It's hard to say. My MIL goes to france to stay with family all the time (she'll be going again soon). Usually on a one way ticket and then they buy her a return ticket later when she decides to go home. She hasn't had any problems that I'm aware of. But countries can refuse to let you enter if they suspect you're not planning to leave.   


I wouldn't tell them you're moving in with her. That will immediately raise questions about your Visa and whether you have enough money, etc., etc.

Anytime your vacation days are near or on Christmas the price is going to go up fairly significantly. If you're looking to save money, my first bit of advice is avoid Christmas, or any holiday really. In any case, I can't imagine a $9k a week all inclusive unless you're booking the most expensive rooms in one of the best hotels or something.  
There aren't any all inclusives in Hawaii that I'm aware of. There are some hotels that offer "packages" but you end up paying a lot to add those packages, making them not so all inclusive really.   
But, in any case, Hawaii is fantastic, Mexico is great (maybe try somewhere in Mexico you haven't been), and Alaska has flights to Costa Rica that are fairly affordable. I think you can get to grand cayman fairly easily as well.

Depending on where you're sailing - you can't feel the ship. The only place I've really felt it was in Alaska. They're huge. 

Most of your complaints seem to be some degree of nervousness and perhaps, just being naturally inclined to complain. In any case, I've had severe anxiety my entire life and I actually feel physically ill before travelling as a result. I love to travel so I just deal with it, and I survive.   


You could die anywhere. At home, while living your routine life....Personally, I'd rather go travelling and doing new things than cowering in my home.   


You do you though.

I think whatever works best for you. I am married. I thought I'd wait to marry until my 30's but ended up getting married in my early 20's and I'm really glad. We have a good relationship. I love my husband and I love being married. I genuinely enjoy our life together. It works for us.

I live in a city/urban area now, but I grew up in a really rural place. Less than 2000 people, no stop lights, no stores, only one gas station...that was literally all. Everything else was farmland, etc.   


My in laws romanticize the rural life and are now in the process of looking to move to a rural area. They're in their late 60's and 70's. I've tried to impress on them that what it actually means to live in a rural area; far from doctors and hospitals, far from grocery stores and pharmacies, etc. Far from help of any kind really. They just don't really understand it and it's not something easy to impart on someone who hasn't lived it. You don't just "run to the store" you "make a run to town". My husband sort of gets this having visited my family many times and done errands with my dad and we've at least convinced them to not move hours away from family, but they are making an offer on a home. I told my husband I fully suspect they're realize that they can't manage it with in a few years and have to sell and do something more practical for people their age. Oh well.   


I'm sure it's easier these days with all the delivery options and texting. I was actually a really early amazon adopter before I moved away because you literally could not even get things I wanted in the neighboring town. The internet was really an asset for getting things and having access to the rest of the world.

I loathe them. They're largely nothing more than gift/cash grabs that have little to nothing to do with welcoming or celebrating the new baby, etc.   


The last one I went to asked for diapers for a diaper raffle, had a gift registry AND then asked for books instead of cards. This is after she has asked her coworkers repeatedly to donate leave since she didn't have enough for her maternity leave. All of that easily adds up to several hundred dollars in gifts and financial support. And we really did nothing more than sit with people we'd never met and ate appetizers, while some people played a few games. It's like light hospitality in exchange for loot.   


I'll not be attending anymore honestly.

Long story short, I'm 37 and recently have developed white coat syndrome. That's when your blood pressure is high when you go to medical appointments, etc, but in actuality your blood pressure is otherwise normal. (In a couple situations where they left me attached to a monitor for awhile it would eventually settled into a normal, healthy range) It started last fall. I'm generally pretty healthy. My anxiety/OCD has been pretty bad lately, and the older I get the more I'm aware that eventually doctors appointments aren't going to be all fine and dandy. I use to never care about going because I've always been pretty healthy. Now my blood pressure goes up and I feel really tense. I'm sure it's because in the back of my head I'm worrying that this is going to be the appointment where I'm not ok. And it sucks. I have a lot of anxiety about my husband's health too. He'll need surgery later this year and I'm stressed just thinking about it.   
I wish I were one of those people who never imagined the bad possibilities. Ignorance really is bliss on some level.

I don't mind flubs. Everyone is human. I have a real hang up over certains sounds though. I HATE whispering, in any context...I hate it. I hate people singing to themselves. And I literally have to change the station if someone has a "wet" sounding voice. There is a female news reporter on NPR who has this issue...she talks about really interesting things, but I actually can't listen. I try, but I always end up having to turn the station until she's gone. I'm pretty sure I have misophonia. I have a cousin who hates the sound of people eating so much they eat alone away from their family at meals.
It went by amazingly fast honestly. It's all sort of a blur.
I stopped watching. The joy of it was gone for me.

The problem I've been see for years is that people like Nate Silver seem to have forgotten that behind those numbers are humans, and humans change. You cannot rely on past voting patterns to predict future ones forever. Especially after an event like an economic calamity that alters society. They fail to look at the psychology of the electorate.   


in 2016 people were sick of establishment people on both sides of the aisle, when Bernie was out a lot of people who just didn't want to vote for another puppet threw in with Trump. I suspect a lot of those people do regret it, or at least are underwhelmed and probably won't show up for him, or at all. But the trauma of 4 years of Trump just muddies the water. Now you have people who just desperately want things to "go back to normal". Biden probably looks super appealing to them. Sanders probably still appeals to people who are desperate for some kind of change that franky, I don't think Biden could or would deliver.   


It's a total crapshoot as far as I can tell.
